content: Metronidazole, when administered orally, has been shown to cause cancer in laboratory animals. It is essential to discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication with your doctor. Metronidazole is prescribed to eliminate bacteria and other microorganisms responsible for infections in the reproductive system, gastrointestinal tract, skin, vagina, and other areas of the body. However, antibiotics like metronidazole are ineffective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Metronidazole is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken two or three times a day for a duration of 5 to 10 days or longer, depending on your doctor’s instructions. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take metronidazole exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Before taking metronidazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to metronidazole or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), astemizole (Hismanal), disulfiram (Antabuse), lithium (Lithobid), phenobarbital, phenytoin (Dilantin), and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had blood disorders, kidney or liver disease, or Crohn's disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking metronidazole, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid consuming alcohol while taking this medication, as it may cause stomach upset, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating, and facial flushing (redness). Additionally, limit unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as metronidazole may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. If you miss a dose of metronidazole, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Metronidazole may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: vomiting, diarrhea, upset stomach, loss of appetite, dry mouth, a sharp or unpleasant metallic taste, dark or reddish-brown urine, a furry tongue, mouth or tongue irritation, or numbness or tingling in the hands or feet. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: rash, itching, stuffy nose, fever, or joint pain. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store metronidazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your response to metronidazole. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still experience symptoms of infection after completing the course of metronidazole, contact your doctor.
